title: TacticzHazel’s Sunday Shoutout #1
content_html:
Happy Sunday to you all,

One of my main goals this year is to improve my writing. And one of the best ways of doing that is by reading more, a lot more. That’s exactly what I’ve been doing in the past months; reading other people’s work here on Substack.

I’ve come across so many small and big Substacks that I really liked, that I figured it would be a waste not to share some of those writers with my own readers.

So here’s what I’ll be doing: I’ll spotlight one creator every Sunday (if it fits my schedule).

It won’t be a long article; it will be just me, telling you what I like about the particular Substack and what articles I would recommend starting with. I’m not gonna bother you with the big names like Citrini and Doomberg, but instead I’ll be focusing on the more niche and smaller creators, so anything under 10k.

I am not getting paid and no one asked me to highlight them. This is just me spreading a bit of love.

Subscribe now

The first Substack that I would like to highlight is Daniel’s Deep Dive.

You might have guessed it already from reading his name, but Daniel writes deep dives. And he writes them well.

In general, he focuses on companies that are quite unfamiliar to the general crowd. While that doesn’t always do wonders for his reach and growth, I think it’s actually what makes him stand out against most other creators here.

He finds unique companies with strong business models, and usually they have a theme behind them with strong tailwinds. It’s a great Substack for idea generation as there’s always a name that you have never heard of.

One of his best articles was one that he did with my Friend Ozeco, also a very good content creator here on Substack. They wrote the most extensive water primer I’ve ever seen—a unique theme that’s still quite undiscovered.

Daniel's Deep DiveWater Primer: The Most Mispriced Resource on Earth and the Defining Investment Theme of the Next Two DecadesTable of Contents…Read more4 months ago · 88 likes · 14 comments · Daniel's Deep Dive and Ozeco

In addition, he has done two other deep dives that I thought were really great. One was Texas Pacific Land, a very unique company that has been around for years, but is really very much under the radar. Truly a beautiful compounder.

Daniel's Deep DiveTexas Pacific Land: A Business That Practically Prints MoneyA few weeks ago I was having dinner with a group of friends who are just as passionate about investing as I am. At some point the conversation shifted to interesting opportunities, and one of them mentioned an American company in the oil and gas space that seemed rather unremarkable at first glance but immediately stood out once he shared its numbers. A…Read more9 months ago · 72 likes · 18 comments · Daniel's Deep Dive

And the second one was a deep dive on Badger Meter, which is a water infrastructure company.

Daniel's Deep DiveBadger Meter: The Future of Water Infrastructure Today we dive into the world of water (pun intended), and more specifically into the future of smart water infrastructure. This industry often flies under the radar, yet it is becoming increasingly important and stands at the beginning of a structural shift, as the need for a safe and efficient water supply reshapes the industry as a whole…Read more8 months ago · 61 likes · 21 comments · Daniel's Deep Dive

He writes in a similar style as myself, it’s not aimed at institutional or academic level investors, but it’s aimed at the regular joe and should be easy enough to understand for everyone.

If you like what I do, you’re sure gonna like what he does.
